title: Problem Overview: Polynomial Interpolation Bound
content:
**Erdős Problem #1133: OPEN**

Can one always choose target values y_i for polynomial interpolation such that ANY approximating polynomial must become large somewhere in [-1,1]?

**The setup:**
- Given sample points x_1,...,x_n in [-1,1]
- Choose target values y_1,...,y_n in [-1,1]
- Consider polynomials P of degree < (1+epsilon)n matching >= (1-epsilon)n points

**The question:** Can we force max |P(x)| > C for any such P?
mathContext: This is about adversarial function approximation. The conjecture asks if we can always 'win' against any polynomial approximation scheme by clever choice of target values.

title: Basic Definitions
content:
**polyEval P x:** P.eval x - polynomial evaluation

**maxNormOnInterval P:** sup_{x in [-1,1]} |P(x)| - the maximum norm on the interval

**SamplePoints n:** Functions from Fin n to [-1,1] representing sample x values

**TargetValues n:** Functions from Fin n to [-1,1] representing target y values

title: Interpolation Conditions
content:
**ApproximatelyInterpolates P x y epsilon:** P passes through at least (1-epsilon)n of the points (x_i, y_i). Allows slack.

**HasBoundedDegree P n epsilon:** deg(P) < (1+epsilon)n. The polynomial has degree slightly less than (1+epsilon)n.

For epsilon = 0, this is exact Lagrange interpolation.

title: The Erdős Conjecture
content:
**ErdosConjecture1133:** For all C > 0, there exists epsilon > 0 such that for large n: for all sample points x_i in [-1,1], there exist target values y_i in [-1,1] such that for all polynomials P with bounded degree and approximate interpolation, max_{[-1,1]} |P| > C.

The quantifier order matters: we choose y_i after seeing x_i, but before seeing P. This is an adversarial game.

title: Erdős's Related Result (Known)
content:
**erdos_related_result:** For any C > 0, there exists epsilon > 0 such that for large n and m = floor((1+epsilon)n) sample points, there EXISTS a polynomial P of degree n with |P(x_i)| <= 1 for all i, yet max |P(x)| > C.

This is WEAKER: it asks for existence of P, not choice of y_i.

title: Lagrange Interpolation
content:
**lagrange_interpolation:** Given n distinct points, there is a unique polynomial of degree < n passing through all.

**lagrange_divergence:** There exist continuous functions for which Lagrange interpolation on uniformly spaced nodes diverges (Runge's phenomenon).

title: Chebyshev Nodes and Optimality
content:
**chebyshevNodes n k:** x_k = cos(pi(2k+1)/(2n)), the optimal nodes for polynomial interpolation.

**chebyshev_optimal:** If P has degree n and |P(x_k)| <= 1 at all Chebyshev nodes, then max |P| <= 1. These nodes minimize the Lebesgue constant.

title: Summary and Main Results
content:
**exact_interpolation_case:** For epsilon = 0 (exact interpolation), Lagrange gives the unique polynomial of degree < n through all n points. Proved from lagrange_interpolation axiom.

**erdos_1133_summary:** Wraps exact_interpolation_case as the main proved result. The conjecture ErdosConjecture1133 remains OPEN.
